newsitem.title: UK: Dollar ends higher in Europe but stg steals show.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends higher in Europe but stg steals show.

text.p: The dollar closed higher against the mark in Europe, shrugging off softer than expected U.S. jobs data and riding higher on the coattails of a recovery in sterling/mark instead.

Sterling hogged the limelight during the European session following Britain's parliamentary elections. The pound recovered from an early profit-taking selloff to levels little changed from where it was before the election as dealers took a calm view of the first Labour government in 18 years.
The only other focus of the day, the April U.S. jobs report, gave mixed signals and pushed the dollar to session lows below 1.72 marks but buying on dips rejuvenated the currency.

"The jobs data weighed on the dollar at first but it has come back nicely since," said Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston in London. "The dollar didn't really have a life of its own today, it was all about sterling."

A mixed non-farm payrolls report showed a modest rise of 142,000 in April and average hourly earnings falling for the fist time in six months, while the jobless rate fell to a 23-year low of 4.9 percent. Economists had expected a rise in non-farm payrolls of 211,000 on average.
Analysts said the jobs data made a decision on interest rates at the next meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-making FOMC a close call.

The unemployment rate dropped to 4.9 percent, the lowest since 1973, from 5.2 percent in March. The key gauge for inflation in the jobs report, average hourly earnings, dipped one cent to $12.14, the first decline in six months.

"The economy almost certainly contracted last month," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic advisor at Bank of America. "This may be enough to prevent the Fed from tightening on May 20 but I still just about go for a 25 basis points hike."
At 1430 GMT the dollar was at 1.7275/85 marks and 125.66/76 yen, compared with 1.7198/03 and 126.60/65 in late European trading on Thursday.
Sterling was at 2.7920/30 marks compared with 2.7935/45 at the previous European close. Against the generally firmer dollar it was at $1.6155/65, down from $1.6253/60.

The pound was sold early in the session as longs were trimmed but bargain-hunters were happy to pick it up at lower levels because the fundamentals that pushed it to 4-1/2 year highs last month remain in favour of the pound.
A Labour victory had been expected but the magnitude of the win caught many by surprise, traders said. Labour is expected to win a majority of about 180 seats in the 659-seat parliament.

Unless the government embarks on a completely different economic course than promised before the election, the pound still has scope to rise, analysts said. "The new government will underline its credibility to the financial markets by raising interest rates very soon," said Paul Lambert, senior currency economist at UBS in London. - Astrid Zweynert, London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
